title: Podman 6 ignores runtime key in containers.conf
body:
### Issue Description

Since updating a Fedora system to F45 and moving from Podman 5.x to Podman 6.x, Podman now silently ignores the runtime setting in containers.conf. I'm running a set of containers on this system with runsc so I've got a containers.conf that looks like this (just the [engine] section):

```
[engine]
runtime = "runsc"

[engine.runtime_flags]
runsc = [
  "platform=kvm",
  "ignore-cgroups",
  "in-sandbox-cgroup=v2"
]
```

I was somewhat concerned to find that after upgrading my system a ton of my containers *silently* started with crun instead of runsc, I only noticed because of some explicit flags I'd set on a couple of containers that blocked crun from starting. This is particularly concerning these days given that the main reason to run an alternative runtime is for stronger isolation and I know I'm far from the only person migrating workloads to hardened runtimes.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Set the runtime= key in containers.conf (not specific to runsc, also happens with at least krun)
2. Run any Podman container in any way (applies to Quadlets, podman-run, podman-build, likely any invocation given the podman system info output)

To prove that this is happening a shortcut way is to call a flag that the target runtime supports that crun doesn't. E.g. the reason I noticed this is that some of my containers run with the additional runtime flag `network=host`, which crun doesn't support. Notably most of the containers I was running silently started with crun instead of runsc because the incompatible runtime flags set in the containers.conf table weren't invoked as Podman mistakenly thought it was supposed to use crun, but the containers using the additional runtime flag have it set explicitly and so tried to pass it to crun and failed to launch.

For the sake of testing I also tried setting an irrelevant flag in the [engine] setup that can be easily checked, setting num_locks = 4096 correctly updates the output of podman system info (reflected in the output below)

### Describe the results you received

Podman silently ignores the setting and launches with crun

podman system info even shows ociRuntime: name: crun

### Describe the results you expected

Podman uses the runtime it's configured to use

On a separate F44 machine, setting the runtime = flag correctly updates the setting and even running podman system info immediately after shows the ociRuntime name changed to the target runtime.

### Additional environment details

I've got 2 Fedora servers, one is still on F44 running Podman 5.8.7 and notably that one works correctly. My F45 system is running 6.1.3, which is *technically* behind upstream but I didn't see any changes in 6.1.4 that would affect containers.conf parsing at least in the changelog.

comments.body:
Podman 6.x parses the [config files](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/main/common/docs/containers-config.5.md) differently than 5.x mainly in the sense that main config files are ranked lower in the order than drop-ins. For instance, Fedora ships a vendor drop-in that sets the runtime to `crun`, SUSE ships with `runc`. These drop-in files are sorted by filename and the last file takes precedence over the previous one. 

So, you should be able to create a drop-in such as `~/.config/containers/containers.conf.d/99-user-runtime.conf` with the runtime attribute set and podman should respect your preferences.

yes ideally all users should just use drop ins

https://blog.podman.io/2026/06/podman-6-configuration-file-changes/
